security.tool: cie-ruleset v1 — AST + line heuristics (not a full SAST scanner)
security.honesty: Eight disclosed rules over the sample's own source. Real static findings with file:line evidence; a production scan would add dataflow analysis and more rules.

rules.name: Hardcoded credential
rules.why: A secret is written in the code. Anyone who reads the repo (or the shipped binary) has it.

rules.name: SQL built by string glue
rules.why: Text glued into SQL lets one input change the query's meaning (SQL injection).

rules.name: Check that always says yes
rules.why: An authorization-looking function that returns True unconditionally protects nothing.

rules.name: Bare except swallows failures
rules.why: A bare except hides real errors (even KeyboardInterrupt) and pretends things worked.

rules.name: Password check without key stretching
rules.why: Plain sha256 is too fast for passwords; stolen hashes can be guessed quickly. bcrypt/argon2 add work.

rules.name: Shell command built from text
rules.why: Text passed to a shell lets input run commands (command injection).

rules.name: Unsafe deserialization
rules.why: pickle.loads on untrusted data can run attacker-chosen code.

rules.name: Weak randomness for security use
rules.why: random (not secrets) is predictable; tokens made from it can be guessed.

derived.proxy_note: defect events = commits whose message says fix/bug (SZZ-style mining). The tracker is empty, so this proxy is what the history can honestly give; MTTR cannot come from commits alone (no close timestamps) — the measured repair loop below covers MTTR.

crash_probe.tool: seeded fuzz harness (cie-probe CRASH-1) — one subprocess per session
crash_probe.definition: crash rate = sessions that ended in an unhandled error (or hang) ÷ all sessions
crash_probe.honesty: Deterministic seeded inputs against the sample's real entry points, run live on this machine. The sample is intentionally flawed, so the rate is high — that is the truth the rest of the data corroborates (same functions the security rules flag).

repair_probe.tool: real fail→fix→recheck loops ×3 (cie-probe MTTR-1), timed with a monotonic clock
repair_probe.mttr_text: 4.49 seconds per repair cycle (mean of 3 really executed cycles)
repair_probe.honesty: The three bugs are scripted, but the executions, the failing test runs and the clocks are real. Production MTTR comes from issue opened→closed times across many defects; this probe measures the mechanical repair leg only.
real_world_equivalents: issue tracker timestamps (opened → closed) for bugs

metrics.name: Defect density
metrics.how_computed_here: 30 fix/bug commits mined from the hosting repository's real 139-commit history ÷ its measured KLOC. The GitHub tracker is empty (recorded as found), so commit mining is the disclosed proxy.
metrics.source: git log --grep + git ls-files line counts; GitHub issues API (empty)

metrics.name: MTTF / MTBF
metrics.typical_calculation: Mean time to failure or between failures
metrics.how_computed_here: Mean interval between the 30 real fix-commit timestamps. The repository was built in a two-day sprint, so gaps are hours — that is what the history honestly gives.

metrics.name: Test coverage
metrics.what_it_measures: How much code is exercised by tests
metrics.value_text: 7.5% of statements touched by the sample's own test run
metrics.how_computed_here: coverage.py measured the sample's real pytest run; the heatmap shows every file, 0% included.

metrics.name: Cyclomatic complexity
metrics.how_computed_here: Real AST walk of every Python function: 1 + decision points (the formula is printed on the chart).

metrics.name: Defect arrival rate
metrics.value_text: 16.0 fix-commits per day over the sprint
metrics.how_computed_here: Fix-commit timestamps bucketed per day across the repository's real two-day history.

metrics.name: Code churn
metrics.value_text: 395544 lines added+deleted across the repository's last 3 active days
metrics.how_computed_here: git log --numstat, per day (hosting repo) and per file (sample), as written by git.

metrics.name: Crash rate
metrics.value_text: 11 of 19 seeded sessions ended in a real crash or hang
metrics.how_computed_here: A deterministic fuzz harness ran the sample's real entry points live, one subprocess per session; unhandled error or hang = crash.

metrics.name: Mean time to repair (MTTR)
metrics.typical_calculation: Average time to resolve a defect
metrics.value_text: 4.49 seconds per repair cycle (mean of 3 really executed cycles)
metrics.how_computed_here: Three real fail→fix→recheck cycles executed and timed during collection (detect + repair + recheck legs).
